intro: Above you rises Alanya Castle, a castle and walls in Antalya province, from the 13th century. This Seljuk fortress wraps the whole peninsula in 6.5 kilometres of wall. Below it, the shipyard and the Red Tower survive from the years when the city was a naval base.
history: In 1221 Alâeddin Keykubad I took the town and made it the Seljuk state's winter seat on the Mediterranean. Then the building began. The 6.5 kilometres of wall around the peninsula went up with more than a hundred towers and hundreds of cisterns. The shipyard below and the Red Tower belong to the years when the navy was built here.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Red Tower and the Shipyard, then climb on to the Inner citadel, the Süleymaniye Mosque and the Arsenal.
facts: Did you know? The five-bay shipyard is the only one the Seljuks built on the Mediterranean coast, and it is still standing eight centuries on. The wall around the peninsula runs 6.5 kilometres and encloses hundreds of cisterns, so under siege the castle collected its own water. And the Red Tower, built to protect the Seljuk shipyard, is the best preserved tower of Anatolian Seljuk military architecture.
outro: This brings our tour of Alanya Castle to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for climbing with us, and enjoy your visit.
